title: AI-Devised Proof Establishes Subexponential Quantum Advantage for Textbook Adiabatic Optimization
aiSystem: GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol & Claude Opus 5
whyItMatters: Settles a 20-year open question: frontier AI models devised a proof that textbook linear-schedule adiabatic optimization achieves subexponential black-box quantum advantage over all classical algorithms.
summary: Posted to arXiv on November 18, 2026 (arXiv:2611.24035) by Yufan Zheng (Visa Research), with an explicit AI contribution table crediting GPT-6 Luna (main strategy), GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Claude Opus 5 with devising the mathematical approach and developing the proof, this paper resolves a ~20-year-old question dating back to Farhi et al.’s original adiabatic quantum optimization (AQO) proposal. Replacing the transverse-field Ising mixer required by earlier 2025 separations with the standard plain transverse-field mixer H_M = −∑ X_i and linear interpolation schedule, the construction proves a family of black-box objective functions f:{0,1}ⁿ → ℝ for which textbook 'vanilla' adiabatic quantum optimization finds the global minimum in poly(n) time while every classical black-box algorithm requires exp(n^Ω(1)) queries.
technicalHighlights: Establishes the first super-quadratic (subexponential) black-box quantum speedup for textbook linear-schedule adiabatic optimization with the standard −∑ X_i transverse-field mixer.
Replaces the Ising-mixer linearization of Leng et al. (2025) with a new AI-devised perturbative reduction preserving polynomial spectral gap.
Explicit AI contribution disclosure documents GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Claude Opus 5 devising the core strategy and proof steps.
caveats: Recent November 2026 preprint awaiting independent peer review; establishes an idealized black-box/oracular separation rather than a direct speedup for noisy hardware on natural combinatorial benchmarks.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves a two-decade theoretical question on whether standard, textbook adiabatic quantum optimization can beat classical algorithms super-quadratically.
scoreRationale.ripple: Clarifies the ultimate complexity-theoretic potential of quantum annealing and adiabatic optimization hardware.
scoreRationale.verification: Complete proof posted to arXiv with transparent AI attribution, currently awaiting independent peer review.
scoreRationale.velocity: Frontier reasoning models devised the exact mixer-elimination reduction that had resisted decades of analysis.
